Mike Rogers

Republican candidate for U.S. Senate, Michigan · Open seat

Former U.S. Representative and former FBI agent; has worked in cybersecurity and national security

Mike Rogers is a former FBI agent and a seven-term former Republican U.S. Representative from Michigan who lives in White Lake Township. He is the Republican nominee for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, who is not seeking a third term. President Donald Trump has endorsed his candidacy.

Where Rogers stands

Trade and tariffs
Calls for an immediate end to the tariff war with Canada, saying 'Canada is not our enemy.' Says some tariffs are working to bring jobs back from Mexico and China.
Immigration and border security
Supports continuing current ICE enforcement. Says it has targeted violent criminals, drug dealers and human traffickers and has had a large impact on crime.
Social Security
Proposes rooting out fraud to address Social Security's projected insolvency. Says fraud prevention could be worth about $500 billion.
Foreign policy / Iran
Says the U.S. war with Iran needs to 'end quickly.'
Economy and cost of living
Says Michiganders are 'hurting' from job losses and high utility bills. Argues that Democratic control of Congress would bring higher taxes and costs, including for gasoline, and says lowering prices is his top priority.

Background

  • FBI special agent (former)
  • U.S. Representative from Michigan, seven terms
  • Has worked in cybersecurity for about a decade since leaving Congress
